text:
A: Hi. Er, can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah. Hiya.
A: I'm Andrew.
B: Leanne.
A: Right. Erm.
B: Go on then, you start.
A: Okay. Er, well, I'm in Beeston, near Nottingham. I do mapping for a water company. Where the pipes are, flood risk, that sort of thing.
B: Is that what all the books are for?
A: Er, no, those are just books. Reading's sort of my thing. And the map on the wall's old Ordnance Survey, Nottinghamshire about 1900. I like seeing what used to be there.
B: Right.
A: What about you?
B: Warehouse. Shift manager, late shift. Normanton, off the M62.
A: Normanton. I've cycled near there, actually. Along the Aire and Calder canal, out past Castleford.
B: You never.
A: Yeah. Leeds and back in a day, sort of a long one. There's a stretch by the river that's nicer than you'd expect.
B: I walk the dog down there most mornings. Before work. That's the only bit of the day that's mine, to be honest. Once I'm in, it's agency not turning up, someone's crashed a reach truck into a racking leg, ops manager's on the phone wanting to know why the pick rate's down. Then I'm not home till gone midnight.
A: That's a long day.
B: It is. I'm knackered most of the time.
A: What sort of dog?
B: Staffy. Bella. She's chewed half the settee cushions, so she's not my favourite this week.
A: We've got a cat. Moss. She's old, she's fine in the day but she wakes me at five every morning for food. Just sits on my chest.
B: That's worse than the dog.
A: I think it might be, yeah.
B: So do you go in an office, or is it just that bedroom?
A: Bit of both. Two days in Nottingham, three here. I prefer here, I suppose. It's quieter. I'm not big on people popping over to your desk.
B: I'd go mad. I can't sit still. I'd rather be on the floor sorting it out myself.
A: Yeah, I'd be rubbish at your job. Forty people shouting at you.
B: How d'you know it's forty?
A: Er, I didn't. I just guessed a big number.
B: It is forty, near enough. You were spot on.
A: Lucky. Erm, do you get rugby where you are? Castleford's a rugby league town, isn't it?
B: Cas Tigers. Dean, that's my partner, and my dad are mad on it. I just end up shouting at the telly with them. I don't even like it that much, but I still get wound up.
A: Same with my dad and Notts County. I go for him really. Sort of sit there in the cold and make the right noises.
B: Is he alright, your dad?
A: Er, mostly. He had a bit of a heart scare last year. He's on tablets now. Still up ladders, which he shouldn't be.
B: Mine had one an' all. Doctors said it were minor, but.
A: Yeah. Doesn't feel minor, does it.
B: No.
A: Is he behaving himself, at least?
B: Is he heck. Still has a fry-up every Saturday. Mam's given up.
A: Mine's started on low-fat spread and moans about it constantly. I think that's the most he'll—
